integration_questions: With wheel_track 0.08 m, does steering_oscillation on the oval rise above about 0.25, or stay near the 0.21 seen in iteration 4?
Does control_effort stay near 7 to 8, or does the narrower track push it higher as the wider sensor array did?
On the slalom, does progress move past the 0.17 to 0.18 plateau? If not, is the stall a turn-rate limit or a lag limit?
Are there any line-loss events at bend entries on the s-bend with the narrower track?

intent: Test whether further turn authority (narrower wheel track, from 0.09 to 0.08 m) raises s-bend progress and reduces off-track ends without losing the oval finishes gained at y=0.08 m. Only wheel_track changes relative to iteration 4. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.5, max_error below 0.06 on the s-bend, at least 17 of 20 oval finishes, and a score above 404.6.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that moving the row to y=0.08 m fixed the oval (20 of 20 finishes) but did not move the slalom, which stays at a progress plateau of about 0.17 to 0.18 across three different designs. The s-bend responds to turn authority, so the next test narrows wheel_track to the 0.08 m minimum. If the slalom still stalls, the limit is probably controller or speed rather than geometry, and the next geometry lever to test is wheel_radius or mass for speed.
rationale: Four races now give a clear picture. Iteration 4 (score 404.6, best so far) moved the 5-sensor row to y=0.08 m with wheel_track 0.09 m. The oval now finishes 20 of 20 (mean 939.8, rms_error 0.023, max_error 0.038), so the forward row fixed the oval's off-track ends from iteration 3. The s-bend improved to progress 0.486 (from 0.446), but it still ends off track at max_error about 0.062. The slalom is flat at progress 0.16 to 0.18 across iterations 1, 3 and 4, and still ends off track at max_error about 0.063 to 0.069. Sensing span was ruled out in iteration 2 (widening to ±0.06 m hurt the oval and raised oscillation), and the forward row is now at its y=0.08 limit, so lookahead cannot go further. Narrowing wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m raised s-bend progress nearly twofold in iteration 3, so turn authority is still the lever that moved the s-bend. I therefore make one change: wheel_track from 0.09 to 0.08 m, the minimum allowed. Everything else stays as in iteration 4 so the effect can be isolated. I expect s-bend progress to rise above 0.5 and max_error to fall below 0.06 on the s-bend, with the oval still finishing most runs. The main risk is that the narrower track adds oscillation or wheel slip on the oval, which earlier cost finishes when the track narrowed to 0.09 m without the forward row. The slalom may stay near 0.17, which would point at a limit other than turn rate.
